senses.gloss: צַיֵּיץ, (Palp. צַיְצֵי) same. Pesik. Dibré, p. 110ᵇ (expl. צהלי, Is. X, 30) צַיְּיצִי בקלך Ar. (ed. Koh. צַיְּצִי; ed. שישי קולך); Yalk. Is. 284 ציצי קולך chirp with thy voice (let thy voice chirp, in studying the Law); v. לַבְלֵב.
units: <cite ref="Niddah 42b:21">Nidd. 42ᵇ</cite> <he>שמעית ולד דצַוֵּיץ וכ׳</he> (Ar. <he>דצייץ</he>) I heard the infant squeak at sunset-time, but it was not born &c.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 12:4">Koh. R. to XII, 4</cite> <he>כד שמע … מְצַוְצְיָין וכ׳</he> (some ed. <he>מצוייצן</he>, corr. acc.) when he hears the birds chirp, he thinks robbers are coming &c.; Yalk. ib. 979 <he>מְצַיְּיצִין</he>.
Lev. R. s. 16 ציפוריא מציצין Ar. (Var., a. ed. קולנין). [Yalk. Is. 281, v. preced.].—Trnsf. (of the singing of boiling water) to boil.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 29b:23">B. Mets. 29ᵇ</cite> <he>אלא דלא צַיֵּיץ</he> only when the water has not been steaming (Ar. <cite ref="M02287"><he>מְצַוְּיָין</he></cite> Ms. F. <he>צַוְיַת</he>; Ms. R. 2 <he>מְצַוְּיַת</he>, v. <cite ref="R00187"><he>צְוֵי</he> I</cite>); <cite ref="Chullin 84b:2">Ḥull. 84ᵇ</cite> <he>צַיֵּיץ</he> Ar. (ed. <cite ref="R00431"><he>צַיֵּץ</he></cite>).
